title: Sternberg Working Memory
description: This dataset contains scalp EEG recordings from 23 healthy young adults performing a Modified Sternberg Working Memory task, in which participants memorized subsets of letters while ignoring others, then responded to probe letters after a maintenance period. The study, conducted at the Swartz Center for Neural Computation (UCSD) in 2004-05, was designed to examine source-resolved EEG brain dynamics related to working memory encoding, maintenance, and retrieval. The dataset was curated and annotated using the Hierarchical Event Descriptors (HED) framework and shared via OpenNeuro and NEMAR in BIDS format.
methods_description: EEG data were collected from 71 electrodes (69 scalp and 2 periocular), referenced to the right mastoid, using a Neurobehavioral Systems EEG system with an analog passband of 0.1-100 Hz. Sampling rates varied across subjects (250 Hz for subjects 1-12, 1000 Hz for subject 14, and 500 Hz for subjects 15-24). Each session consisted of 3-4 task blocks of 25 trials, with each trial involving letter sequence presentation, a memory maintenance period, a memory probe, and auditory feedback on response accuracy.
